source_name: UK Find a Tender service (OCDS 1.1 release packages)
rate_limits: UNKNOWN - no published numeric limit found; 6-request probe at 0.8 s interval was never throttled
licence: Open Government Licence v3.0 for UK public sector information (documented by the publisher); notice-level attribution required
update_frequency: continuous (releases are appended as procurements progress; the probe returned a release published 2026-11-08T20:14:58Z)
historical_coverage: OCDS releases for UK above-threshold procurements; exact start date not verified in this probe
timestamp_fields: awards[].date (populated in the schema but null in the probed records)
release.tag is the stage marker: ['tender'] vs ['award','contract']
known_limitations: No keyword/company parameter on the OCDS feed: adding `keywords` returns HTTP 400. Firm-level retrieval must therefore go through the HTML search page, which is not a documented record API, or through a date-windowed full scan.

release.date is the release's publication/update timestamp, not necessarily the first time the procurement became public; a re-published release carries a later date. First-observation semantics need the earliest release of an ocid, which requires walking the ocid's history.
awards[].date was null in every probed record, so the award date is not usable as event_at; contracts[].dateSigned is the reliable signature date.
bids/parties may be redacted for some procedures; tender.items carry only CPV classification and delivery regions, never a device model or UDI, so no product-level join is possible.
Coverage is UK above-threshold procurement as published on FTS; below-threshold and pre-FTS historical contracts are not here.

bulk_download_available is PARTIAL: the OCDS feed is a paged bulk-style feed (limit/updatedFrom/updatedTo), not a downloadable archive. Full-country extraction requires a long paged walk within rate limits.
research_value: The strongest procurement source verified in this batch for the notice->award->contract chain: releases are stage-tagged, awards name the supplier with an OCDS organisation id, and contracts carry dateSigned plus a GBP value. It lets MedRadar observe a public tender first, then the same procurement being awarded, then the contract signature date - three separate dates, not one.
cost_notes: free; no key; paged feed rather than a single archive
